note: This slice makes the session-start gate ritual fast in two ways. (1) SnapshotdClient.health() in snapshotd_client.py now opens its gRPC channel with a short 0.3s connect timeout so the liveness probe fails fast when snapshotd is OFF instead of waiting the 5.0s default connect timeout. This is an in-place I/O-timeout change on an existing Python method: the dead time was a network connect wait, not CPU work, so there is no compute-Python hot loop that a native (C++/Go/Rust) rewrite could speed up. (2) The startupd gate handler in handler.go gains a small mutex-guarded 45s TTL cache that re-signs the HMAC token on every request; this is NEW Go code, already in a fast systems language, not a Python compute path. python_lines_remaining=0 means 'compute-Python lines warranting a native rewrite', which is correct here: the only Python touched is an I/O-bound error/connect path, and the cache is already native Go. A further language rewrite gives no measurable gain and would only add a cross-language boundary.

baseline.function: SnapshotdClient.health post-fix (session-start snapshot liveness probe, after the 0.3s connect-timeout fix)
baseline.workload: post-fix wall-clock of the snapshot health probe; the remaining time is the network connect/socket wait (I/O bound), not CPU compute. This baseline measures what a further native (C++/Go/Rust) rewrite of the remaining touched code would start from.
